The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: A plate of the Russian Menaion Reader (Жития Святых, 1903–1911), whose file names carry the church-year date: «11141» is church-month 11 = July, day 14, plate 1. The 14 July Julian is this folder's own Russian and Serbian feast day, and the plate is titled «Акила» — the exact Russian name form this folder already stores. The only other plate on that day is «Еллий», a different man. Not the Greek 14 July «Άγιος Ακύλας» of `aquila-14-july`: that saint has no Russian day and no Russian Lives entry, and this plate stands in the Russian book on the Russian day, which is the apostle of the Seventy. Commons describes it: Иллюстрации к книге: Жития святых на русском языке, изложенные по руководству Четьих-Миней  с дополнениями, объяснительными примечаниями и изображениями святых
